principle: Direct harm, displacement, and civilian resource loss remain separate observed components. No post-hoc scalar composite is permitted.
record_unit: One source-supported claim at the narrowest jointly supported component, victim class, date interval, geography, and attribution scope.

rules: Deaths, injuries, and total casualties are never silently converted into one another.
If a source reports only total casualties, the death/injury split is UNKNOWN unless separately identified by that source or an independently frozen linkage rule.
Victim status must be explicitly civilian under the source's own classification rule; total battle deaths are inadmissible without a civilian classification.
Source-native disputed, probable, verified, alleged, or minimum counts remain distinguishable.
Flow, stock, and return measures are separate and cannot be summed as one quantity.
Internal displacement and cross-border refuge remain separate components.
Generic migration is excluded unless conflict/policy displacement is identified by the source.
A later IDP stock cannot be back-allocated across earlier dates without an independently frozen stock-flow reconstruction.
Physical counts, currency values, land area, livestock, crop loss, and other native units remain separate unless a prospective valuation operator is independently justified.
Organization resource acquisition is not automatically civilian resource loss; the civilian-side loss must be observed or explicitly represented.
Taxation is not coded as harm solely because an armed actor levied it; coercive seizure/loss requires source-supported victim-side cost semantics.

missingness_and_uncertainty.rule: Use source-reported point/range values when available. If the source gives qualitative uncertainty only, preserve that qualitatively and leave unsupported numeric bounds blank rather than fabricating precision.
missingness_and_uncertainty.open_interval_rule: Minimum/at-least counts use the reported value as a lower bound with no invented upper bound; maximum/at-most counts analogously retain only an upper bound.
missingness_and_uncertainty.classification_uncertainty_rule: Civilian-status or actor-attribution uncertainty is coded separately from count uncertainty and cannot be collapsed into an arbitrary numeric discount.

time_operator.rule: A claim covering an interval contributes only to comparisons whose declared temporal operator can consume interval-censored evidence; otherwise it remains unscored.

spatial_operator.rule: National, province/district, locality, facility, and route-level observations remain at source-supported resolution. Aggregation is allowed only upward through a prospectively declared, complete-enough coverage operator.

attribution_operator.rule: Preserve source attribution. Do not infer perpetrator from territorial control, event type, geography, or Pineland state.
attribution_operator.policy_harm_rule: Policy-attributable harm is a separate pathway from combat harm and requires explicit intervention/policy attribution.

source_dependence_and_overlap.rule: Potentially overlapping reports are not added together unless event/person identity or a source-declared de-duplication rule establishes non-overlap. Cross-source agreement is evidence about measurement, not permission to double count.

aggregation_and_comparison.allowed_direct_harm_rate: civilian direct harm per 100000 represented civilian person-years only when numerator semantics match and denominator coverage is identified
aggregation_and_comparison.displacement_reporting: persons, represented population share, or source-native stock/flow rate as separately registered
aggregation_and_comparison.resource_loss_reporting: source-native units until a separate valuation contract exists
forbidden: combining injuries and deaths via post-hoc severity weights
converting resource loss to casualty equivalents
using violence as missing civilian harm
using Pineland fit to choose aggregation level

first_coder_gate.required_next_step: Populate a source-bound first-coder table, then build a blind second-coder packet before adjudication.
